thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD_RULE=region-az2-serving-latency-high (severity: P1) -> triggered 4:13 UTC. Affected service: inference-hosting-az2. Auto-retries: 3.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #INC6274123456 created and routed to "Amelia (on-call)". Escalation timer: 5m.

Amelia (on-call): ack. digging in. first pass: confirm customer impact and whether autopager fallback already kicked.

Jules: I see a spike on node e3f-az2-gpu-11: token latency tails up to 2s and 5xx rate creeping from 0.3% -> 2.1%.

Sanjay: copying metrics: host-level CPU steady, network p95 increased across the shard group. can't rule out noisy neighbor eviction.

Amelia (on-call): good detail. @pagerduty, did the autopager attempt diversion? incident-bot: can you paste the fallback activation log?

incident-bot: autopager: fallback-check -> NO_FALLBACK_TRIGGERED. reason: capacity threshold not crossed. routing-policy: latency-first.

Lynn (Support): we have 3 customer tickets inbound about slower responses (apps show spinner > 3s). low volume but visible to a small set of premium customers. Flagging as potential SLO breach.

Amelia (on-call): ok prioritize mitigation to reduce p95. Quick plan: 1) try soft divert to az1 region for low-risk routes, 2) increase pod replicas for az2 serving pool by +20% via autoscale override, 3) enable model-variant fallback (quantized) for non-production traffic. executing step 2 now.

Jules: running override:
```bash
kubectl scale deployment/inference-az2-serving --replicas=18 -n redwood-serving
```
Doing a rolling scale; watching pods come up.

Sanjay: I'm starting a rolling drain check on e3f-az2-gpu-11 to see if eviction + rebalancing helps. will cordon if necessary.

ml-runner: we can switch a small percentage (5%) of requests to the 8-bit quantized variant; it reduces per-token latency but slightly changes output. need product approval for customer-facing models.

Kai (Product): ok for now to use quantized fallback for non-SL rule routes and for customers outside the strict SLA group. Lynn — coordinate messaging if any premium customers are affected.

Amelia (on-call): enabling quantized variant for control route set CR-low-risk (5%). command:
```json
{"route": "cr-low-risk", "model_variant": "v1-8bit-quant", "traffic_pct": 5}
```
Applied.

incident-bot: autoscale override accepted, new target replicas=18. Pod readiness: 12/18 ready (2m).

Jules: after scale p95 dropped from 920ms -> 420ms on the scaled group. global p95 still ~700ms because a subset of shards still behind.

Sanjay: cordoned e3f-az2-gpu-11 and evicted non-critical pods. There's a rebalancing in progress. Watching KV cache regen.

Lynn (Support): I updated the customer-facing tracker: "We are investigating a regional latency issue in AZ2; some requests may be slower. Root cause under investigation."

Amelia (on-call): sending traffic diversion to az1 for 10% of burst traffic to relieve tail. command: route weight change
```bash
redwoodctl route update --route default --region-weights az2=90,az1=10
```
Applied.

incident-bot: route update applied. New distribution: az2=90%, az1=10%.

Jules: perf after route change: az2 p95 -> 380ms, az1 p95 -> 300ms. global p95 -> 360ms. error rate trending down.

Amelia (on-call): good. keep autoscale override until stabilization. action item: check KV cache warmup to prevent repeated spikes. Sanjay, any signs of repeated cache evictions?

Sanjay: KV cache eviction spikes align with node OOM events on the previous day; node memory pressure now nominal. I'm watching mem-usage; no further OOMs for 12m.

ml-runner: note: the quantized variant introduced tiny diffs on a small eval set, no regression flagged yet. recommend keeping at 5% for now while we finish healing.

Kai (Product): thumbs up. let's not expand quantized traffic beyond this until we confirm evaluation.

Lynn (Support): only 2 customers still reporting slowness, both non-critical tenants; I've DM'd them and offered a status note.

Jules: Pod readiness stabilized at 18/18. rebalanced KV reads match prior baseline.

Amelia (on-call): I'm going to step down from heavy ops in 10m; handing off to Jules for on-call until fully resolved. Jules, you are the primary now — please ack.

Jules: ack. taking over.

pagerduty: Amelia (on-call) acknowledged the incident at 4:14 UTC. Jules has taken primary ownership at 4:25 UTC. Escalation timers reset.

incident-bot: automated health-checks passing post-mitigation: 4 consecutive green checks.

Jules: monitoring for 15m more. if stable, we will 1) remove autoscale override to normal policy, 2) rollback route weight to az2=100%, 3) keep quantized variant at 5% for 1h then reevaluate.

Sanjay: agree. KV cache hit ratio returned to 98% after rebalancing.

Lynn (Support): I'll update public tracker: "Mitigation in place; we see latency improvements. Monitoring continues."

Amelia (on-call): final ask: please file a post-incident note with timeline and root-candidate list: node memory pressure -> KV cache churn -> tail latency. I'll start a stub doc.

Jules: will do. marking incident as 'mitigated' for customer impact (no hard SLO breaches observed yet). Moving to "monitoring".

pagerduty: Incident #INC6274123456 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

ml-runner: opened follow-up ticket: ML-827: evaluate quantized variant drift at 5% traffic; run batch eval.

Amelia (on-call): handing back to normal rotations. Great quick work everyone. :thumbsup:

Lynn (Support): posting final customer note in 5m.

Jules: closing monitoring window at 4:53 UTC. we'll keep the autoscale override in place for +10m then revert if stable.

Amelia (on-call): incident closed in PagerDuty (ack -> resolved) at 4:55 UTC. please add any postmortem comments to the incident doc.

Jules: postmortem outline created: root-candidate, timeline, mitigations, action items (node memory alerts tuning, autopager threshold review, cache warmup improvements).

Kai (Product): thanks all. coordinate with support on any customer follow-ups.

incident-bot: Incident #INC6274123456 resolved. auto-close timer started (24h review window).
